paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the good life can make you forget the One who gave it. Israel had pasture, and the text says, "When they had pasture, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, their hearts became proud, and as a result they forgot Me." (Hosea 13:6) Look at the steps in that verse: pasture, satisfied, proud, forgot. I think that's the sneaky part, because a full belly doesn't feel like danger.

And the LORD doesn't say this to be cruel. He reminds them, "I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me." (Hosea 13:4) Idols made from their own silver could not save them, and the passage says those who trust in them will vanish like morning mist (Hosea 13:3). That's a hard word, and I think this passage is heavy. But the LORD is telling the truth about who can actually help, and it's Him.

Right in the middle of the warning, a promise breaks through: "I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death." (Hosea 13:14) So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery: when life is good, remember the One who gave it. And when you've drifted, remember the One who ransoms. Keep your ovens warm and your heart close to Him, baker. The story isn't over.
